description: This topic explores the importance of water to crops, sources of farm water, methods of irrigation, drainage, and ways of conserving water in farming.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best explains why water is important to growing crops?

options.text: It dissolves and transports nutrients within the plant
It increases the weight of the soil
It changes the colour of the leaves to dark green permanently
It removes all weeds from the field

mcq.explanation: Water acts as a solvent and medium for transporting dissolved mineral nutrients from the soil to all parts of the plant.

mcq.questionText: Irrigation can best be defined as the:

options.text: Removal of excess water from a waterlogged field
Artificial application of water to crops or soil
Natural falling of rain on farmland
Spraying of pesticides on crops

mcq.explanation: Irrigation is the artificial supply of water to crops or soil to supplement rainfall, especially when rain is insufficient.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a natural source of water for agriculture?

options.text: Water tank
Borehole pump
River
Concrete canal

mcq.explanation: Rivers, lakes, rainfall and springs are natural sources of water, while tanks, pumps and canals are man-made structures.

mcq.questionText: In which irrigation method is water allowed to flow along small channels between crop rows?

options.text: Drip irrigation
Furrow irrigation
Sprinkler irrigation
Sub-surface irrigation

mcq.explanation: In furrow irrigation water runs through shallow channels (furrows) dug between rows of crops and soaks into the ridges.

mcq.questionText: Which irrigation method applies water to the soil drop by drop directly at the plant roots?

options.text: Basin irrigation
Sprinkler irrigation
Drip irrigation
Flood irrigation

mcq.explanation: Drip (trickle) irrigation delivers water slowly, drop by drop, through pipes and emitters near the plant roots.

mcq.questionText: Which irrigation method most closely imitates natural rainfall?

options.text: Sprinkler irrigation
Furrow irrigation
Basin irrigation
Surface irrigation

mcq.explanation: Sprinkler irrigation sprays water into the air through nozzles so that it falls onto crops like rain.

mcq.questionText: The main advantage of drip irrigation over surface irrigation is that it:

options.text: Wets the whole field uniformly including paths
Uses water very efficiently with little wastage
Requires no equipment at all
Encourages rapid weed growth

mcq.explanation: Because water is delivered directly to the roots, drip irrigation reduces losses from evaporation and runoff, saving water.

mcq.questionText: A major disadvantage of sprinkler irrigation is that it:

options.text: Cannot be used on uneven land
Loses much water through evaporation, especially in strong wind
Always causes waterlogging
Cannot apply fertilizers

mcq.explanation: Since sprinklers throw water into the air, a lot can be lost through evaporation and wind drift before reaching the soil.

mcq.questionText: Basin irrigation is most suitable for which type of crops?

options.text: Closely spaced cereals on flat land
Fruit trees grown individually
Crops grown on very steep slopes
Crops requiring very little water

mcq.explanation: In basin irrigation a small bank is built around each tree to hold water, making it well suited to individually spaced fruit trees.

mcq.questionText: Drainage in agriculture refers to the:

options.text: Addition of water to dry soil
Removal of excess water from the soil
Mixing of manure into the soil
Covering of soil with mulch

mcq.explanation: Drainage is the process of removing excess or stagnant water from waterlogged soils to improve aeration and crop growth.

mcq.questionText: Why is good drainage important on a waterlogged farm?

options.text: It improves air supply to the roots
It removes all nutrients from the soil
It makes the soil permanently dry and dusty
It increases the number of weeds

mcq.explanation: Removing excess water allows air to enter the soil so that roots and soil organisms can respire properly.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a method of conserving water in farming?

options.text: Leaving the soil bare during the dry season
Covering the soil with mulch
Watering crops at midday when it is hottest
Removing all trees from the farm

mcq.explanation: Mulching covers the soil surface and reduces evaporation, thereby conserving soil moisture for the crops.

mcq.questionText: A farmer with a small water supply on hilly, uneven land would benefit MOST from which irrigation method?

options.text: Furrow irrigation
Basin irrigation
Drip irrigation
Flood irrigation

mcq.explanation: Drip irrigation uses little water and works well on uneven or sloping ground since it does not rely on water flowing across the surface.

mcq.questionText: Which statement about surface (flood) irrigation is correct?

options.text: It is cheap to set up but can waste a lot of water
It requires expensive pumps and pipes for every plant
It applies water drop by drop
It cannot be used on flat land

mcq.explanation: Surface irrigation is low-cost and simple, but large amounts of water are lost through deep percolation, runoff and evaporation.

mcq.questionText: Continuous over-irrigation of a field is most likely to cause:

options.text: Better aeration of the soil
Waterlogging and poor root growth
An increase in soil temperature
A reduction in soil salinity in all cases

mcq.explanation: Applying too much water fills soil pores and removes air, leading to waterlogging that suffocates and weakens plant roots.

fib.questionText: The artificial application of water to crops or soil is called _____.
fib.explanation: Irrigation supplements rainfall by supplying water to crops artificially.

fib.questionText: The removal of excess water from waterlogged soil is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Drainage improves soil aeration by removing stagnant water.

fib.questionText: In _____ irrigation, water flows along small channels dug between rows of crops.
fib.explanation: Furrow irrigation moves water through channels between crop ridges.

fib.questionText: The irrigation method that supplies water to the roots drop by drop is called _____ irrigation.
fib.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water slowly through emitters near plant roots, saving water.

fib.questionText: The irrigation method that sprays water into the air like rainfall is called _____ irrigation.
fib.explanation: Sprinkler irrigation distributes water through nozzles in a rain-like manner.

fib.questionText: Covering the soil surface with dry plant material to reduce evaporation is called _____.
fib.explanation: Mulching conserves soil moisture by reducing water loss through evaporation.

fib.questionText: A natural underground source of water reached by digging or drilling a hole is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Wells and boreholes tap into underground water for use on the farm.

fib.questionText: In basin irrigation, a small _____ is built around each tree to hold water.
fib.explanation: A raised bank or ridge keeps the water within the basin around the tree.

fib.questionText: Water is essential for the process of _____ by which green plants make their own food.
fib.explanation: Plants use water together with carbon dioxide and sunlight to make food during photosynthesis.

fib.questionText: A soil that holds too much water and lacks air for plant roots is said to be _____.
fib.explanation: Waterlogged soils have their pore spaces filled with water, removing the air roots need.

tf.questionText: Irrigation is the artificial application of water to crops to supplement rainfall.
tf.explanation: Irrigation supplies extra water to crops when rainfall is insufficient.

tf.questionText: Drainage means adding more water to dry soil.
tf.explanation: Drainage is the removal of excess water from the soil, not the addition of water.

tf.questionText: Drip irrigation generally uses water more efficiently than surface irrigation.
tf.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to roots, reducing losses from evaporation and runoff.

tf.questionText: Rivers and lakes are man-made sources of water for agriculture.
tf.explanation: Rivers and lakes are natural sources; dams, tanks and canals are man-made.

tf.questionText: Sprinkler irrigation can lose a lot of water through evaporation on hot, windy days.
tf.explanation: Water sprayed into the air can evaporate or be blown away before reaching the soil.

tf.questionText: Water helps to transport dissolved nutrients from the soil to the leaves of a plant.
tf.explanation: Water carries dissolved minerals up the plant through the transport tissues.

tf.questionText: Mulching increases water loss from the soil by evaporation.
tf.explanation: Mulching reduces evaporation and therefore conserves soil moisture.

tf.questionText: Furrow irrigation requires water to flow along channels between crop rows.
tf.explanation: In furrow irrigation water runs through shallow channels dug between the crop rows.

tf.questionText: Continuous over-irrigation can lead to waterlogging of the soil.
tf.explanation: Too much water fills the soil pores and removes the air that roots need, causing waterlogging.

tf.questionText: Surface irrigation is usually more expensive to set up than drip irrigation.
tf.explanation: Surface irrigation is generally cheaper and simpler, while drip systems need pipes and emitters that cost more.

summary.correctAnswer: Artificial application of water to crops or soil
summary.explanation: It supplements rainfall when natural rain is not enough.

summary.correctAnswer: It dissolves and transports nutrients and is used in photosynthesis
summary.explanation: Water keeps plant cells firm and supports food-making and growth.

summary.correctAnswer: Rivers, lakes, rainfall, springs and underground water
summary.explanation: These occur in nature without being built by people.

summary.correctAnswer: Dams, tanks, canals, boreholes and wells
summary.explanation: These are structures built to store or supply water for farming.

summary.correctAnswer: Water flows through channels dug between crop rows
summary.explanation: It is simple and cheap but can waste water.

summary.correctAnswer: Water is supplied drop by drop to the plant roots
summary.explanation: It saves water and suits dry areas and uneven land.

summary.correctAnswer: Water is sprayed into the air to fall on crops like rain
summary.explanation: It can lose water through evaporation in wind and heat.

summary.correctAnswer: Removal of excess water from the soil
summary.explanation: It improves soil aeration and prevents waterlogging.

summary.correctAnswer: It improves air supply to roots and prevents waterlogging
summary.explanation: Well-drained soil allows healthy root growth and farm operations.

summary.correctAnswer: Practices like mulching, drip irrigation and tree planting reduce water loss
summary.explanation: These methods keep moisture in the soil and use water efficiently.

hoq.questionText: A farmer in a dry region has limited water and grows tomatoes on sandy soil. Which irrigation method and reason is the BEST choice?

options.text: Flood irrigation, because it covers the whole field quickly
Drip irrigation, because it delivers water directly to roots with little loss
Sprinkler irrigation, because it wets the leaves and the paths
Basin irrigation, because tomatoes are large trees

hoq.explanation: With scarce water and fast-draining sandy soil, drip irrigation minimises losses and supplies water steadily to the roots, making it the most efficient choice.

hoq.questionText: Two farmers use the same amount of water, but one mulches the soil and the other leaves it bare. Why does the mulching farmer's crops survive the dry spell better?

options.text: Mulch adds extra water to the soil
Mulch reduces evaporation so more moisture stays in the soil
Mulch heats the soil and speeds up drying
Mulch stops the roots from absorbing water

hoq.explanation: Mulch shades and covers the soil surface, lowering evaporation, so the moisture already in the soil remains available to the crops for longer.

hoq.questionText: A flat field beside a river keeps becoming waterlogged after heavy rains, and the maize roots are turning yellow and rotting. What is the most appropriate solution?

options.text: Add more irrigation water to the field
Construct drainage channels to remove the excess water
Plant the maize more closely together
Cover the whole field with thick plastic sheeting

hoq.explanation: The roots are suffering from lack of air due to waterlogging, so digging drainage channels to remove excess water restores soil aeration and healthy root growth.
